sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2\hat{\mathrm{j}}+3\hat{\mathrm{k}}$

$\vec{\mathrm{b}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+2\hat{\mathrm{k}}$

$\vec{\mathrm{c}}=\hat{5\mathrm{i}}-3\hat{\mathrm{j}}+3\hat{\mathrm{k}}$

$(\vec{\mathrm{r}}-\vec{\mathrm{c}})\times ⃗{b}=0,⃗{r}\cdot ⃗{a}=0$

$\Rightarrow ⃗{r}-⃗{c}=λ⃗{b}$

Also, $(⃗{c}+λ⃗{b})\cdot ⃗{a}=0$

$\Rightarrow ⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}+λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b})=0$

$\therefore λ=\frac{⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}}{⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}}=\frac{-8}{5}$

$\vec{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{5(5\hat{\mathrm{i}}-3\hat{\mathrm{i}}+3\hat{\mathrm{k}})-8(\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+2\hat{\mathrm{k}})}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{17\hat{\mathrm{i}}-7\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{\mathrm{r}}|^{2}=\frac{1}{25}(289+50)$

$\Rightarrow$ $25|\vec{\mathrm{r}}|^{2}=339$

text: The equation $\mathrm{e}^{4x}+8\mathrm{e}^{3x}+13\mathrm{e}^{2x}-8\mathrm{e}^{x}+1=0,x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ has :
options: two solutions and both are negative
two solutions and only one of them is negative
four solutions two of which are negative
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$e^{4x}+8e^{3x}+13e^{2x}-8e^{x}+1=0$

Let $\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{t}$

Now, $\mathrm{t}^{4}+8\mathrm{t}^{3}+13\mathrm{t}^{2}-8\mathrm{t}+1=0$

Dividing equation by $\mathrm{t}^{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} t^{2}+8t+13-\dfrac{8}{t}+\dfrac{1}{t^{2}}=0 \\  \\ t^{2}+\dfrac{1}{t^{2}}+8\left (t-\dfrac{1}{t}\right )+13=0 \\  \\ \left (t-\dfrac{1}{t}\right )^{2}+2+8\left (t-\dfrac{1}{t}\right )+13=0 \end{array}$

Let $\mathrm{t}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{z}$

$z^{2}+8z+15=0$

$\begin{array}{l} (z+3)(z+5)=0 \end{array}$

$z=-3\text{or}z=-5$

So, $\mathrm{t}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}=-3$ or $\mathrm{t}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}=-5$

$t^{2}+3t-1=0$ or $t^{2}+5t-1=0$

$\mathrm{t}=\frac{-3\pm \sqrt{13}}{2}$ or $\mathrm{t}=\frac{-5\pm \sqrt{29}}{2}$

as $t=e^{x}$ so $t$ must be positive,

$t=\frac{\sqrt{13}-3}{2}\text{or}\frac{\sqrt{29}-5}{2}$

So, $x=\ln \left (\frac{\sqrt{13}-3}{2}\right )$ or $x=\ln \left (\frac{\sqrt{29}-5}{2}\right )$

Hence two solutions and both are negative.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Let $α>0$. If $\int\limits _{0}^{α}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+α}-\sqrt{x}}\mathrm{d}x=\frac{16+20\sqrt{2}}{15}$, then $α$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int\limits _{0}^{α}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+α}-\sqrt{x}}dx,α>0$

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{1}{α}\int\limits _{0}^{α}x(\sqrt{x+α}+\sqrt{x})dx \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & =\dfrac{1}{α}\int\limits _{0}^{α}\left (x\sqrt{x+α}+x\sqrt{x}\right )dx \\  & =\dfrac{1}{α}\int\limits _{0}^{α}\left [(x+α-α)\sqrt{x+α}+x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]dx \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{1}{α}\int\limits _{0}^{α}\left [(x+α)^{3/2}-α(x+α)^{1/2}+x^{3/2}\right ]dx \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{α}\left [\dfrac{2}{5}(x+α)^{5/2}-α\dfrac{2}{3}(x+α)^{3/2}+\dfrac{2}{5}x^{5/2}\right ]_{0}^{α} \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{α}\left (\dfrac{2}{5}(2α)^{5/2}-\dfrac{2α}{3}(2α)^{3/2}+\dfrac{2}{5}α^{5/2}-\dfrac{2}{5}α^{5/2}+\dfrac{2}{3}α^{5/2}\right ) \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{α}\left (\dfrac{2^{7/2}α^{5/2}}{5}-\dfrac{2^{5/2}α^{5/2}}{3}+\dfrac{2}{3}α^{5/2}\right )=α^{3/2}\left (\dfrac{2^{7/2}}{5}-\dfrac{2^{5/2}}{3}+\dfrac{2}{3}\right ) \\  \\ =\dfrac{α^{3/2}}{15}(24\sqrt{2}-20\sqrt{2}+10)=\dfrac{α^{3/2}}{15}(4\sqrt{2}+10) \end{array}$

Now, $\frac{α^{3/2}}{15}(4\sqrt{2}+10)=\frac{16+20\sqrt{2}}{15}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}(4\sqrt{2}+10)}{15}$

$\Rightarrow α^{3/2}=2\sqrt{2}=2^{3/2}$

$\Rightarrow α=2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

solution.body:
$a_{7}=3\Rightarrow a+6d=3\Rightarrow a=3-6d$

$\begin{array}{l} a_{1}\cdot a_{4}=a(a+3d) \\  \\ \Rightarrow (3-6d)(3-6d+3d) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3(1-2d)3(1-d) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 9\left (2d^{2}-3d+1\right ) \end{array}$

Let $f(d)=2d^{2}-3d+1$

$f^{'}(d)=4d-3\Rightarrow d=\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore a=3-6\cdot \frac{3}{4}=3-\frac{9}{2}=-\frac{3}{2}$

$S_{n}=0$

$\frac{n}{2}(2a+(n-1)d)=0$

$\Rightarrow 2\cdot \left (-\frac{3}{2}\right )+(n-1)\left (\frac{3}{4}\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow \quad 3=\frac{3}{4}(n-1)$

$\Rightarrow n=5$

Now, $n!-4\cdot a_{n(n+2)}$

$\begin{array}{l} =5!-4\cdot a_{35} \\  \\ =120-4\left (-\dfrac{3}{2}+34\cdot \dfrac{3}{4}\right ) \\  \\ =120-(-6+102) \\  \\ =120-(96) \\  \\ =24 \end{array}$

text: $\lim _{x\to \infty }\frac{(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{3x-1})^{6}+(\sqrt{3x+1}-\sqrt{3x-1})^{6}}{\left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right )^{6}+\left (x-\sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right )^{6}}x^{3}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Taking out the dominant powers of $x$:

$(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{3x-1})^{6}+(\sqrt{3x+1}-\sqrt{3x-1})^{6}=x^{3}\left [\left (\sqrt{3+\frac{1}{x}}+\sqrt{3-\frac{1}{x}}\right )^{6}+\left (\sqrt{3+\frac{1}{x}}-\sqrt{3-\frac{1}{x}}\right )^{6}\right ]$

$\left (x+\sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right )^{6}+\left (x-\sqrt{x^{2}-1}\right )^{6}=x^{6}\left [\left (1+\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{x^{2}}}\right )^{6}+\left (1-\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{x^{2}}}\right )^{6}\right ]$

With the extra factor $x^{3}$, the powers of $x$ cancel: $\dfrac{x^{3}\cdot x^{3}}{x^{6}}=1$.

As $x\to \infty$, the first bracket tends to $(2\sqrt{3})^{6}+0$ and the second to $2^{6}+0$, so the limit is

$\frac{(2\sqrt{3})^{6}}{2^{6}}=\left (\sqrt{3}\right )^{6}=27$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation 

$\left (3y^{2}-5x^{2}\right )y\mathrm{d}x+2x\left (x^{2}-y^{2}\right )\mathrm{d}y=0$ 

such that $y(1)=1$. Then $\left |(y(2))^{3}-12y(2)\right |$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The equation gives

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y(5x^{2}-3y^{2})}{2x(x^{2}-y^{2})},$

which is homogeneous. Put $y=mx$:

$m+x\dfrac{dm}{dx}=\dfrac{m(5-3m^{2})}{2(1-m^{2})}\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dm}{dx}=\dfrac{m(3-m^{2})}{2(1-m^{2})}.$

Separating the variables and using partial fractions,

$\dfrac{dx}{x}=\dfrac{2(m^{2}-1)}{m(m^{2}-3)}dm=\left (\dfrac{2}{3m}+\dfrac{4m}{3(m^{2}-3)}\right )dm.$

Integrating,

$\ln |x|=\dfrac{2}{3}\ln |m|+\dfrac{2}{3}\ln |m^{2}-3|+C\Rightarrow |m(m^{2}-3)|=k|x|^{3/2}.$

At $x=1$, $y=1$: $m=1$ and $|1-3|=k$, so $k=2$. With $m=\dfrac{y}{x}$ and $x>0$:

$\left |\dfrac{y(y^{2}-3x^{2})}{x^{3}}\right |=2x^{3/2}\Rightarrow \left |y^{3}-3x^{2}y\right |=2x^{9/2}.$

At $x=2$:

$\left |(y(2))^{3}-12y(2)\right |=2\cdot 2^{9/2}=2\cdot 16\sqrt{2}=32\sqrt{2}.$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: The set of all values of $a^{2}$ for which the line $x+y=0$ bisects two distinct chords drawn from a point $\mathrm{P}\left (\frac{1+a}{2},\frac{1-a}{2}\right )$ on the circle $2x^{2}+2y^{2}-(1+a)x-(1-a)y=0$, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dividing by $2$, the circle is $x^{2}+y^{2}-2hx-2ky=0$ with $h=\dfrac{1+a}{4}$, $k=\dfrac{1-a}{4}$; its centre is $(h,k)$ and $P$ is $(2h,2k)$.

Let a chord through $P$ have its midpoint $M(λ,-λ)$ on $x+y=0$. By $T=S_{1}$, the chord is

$λx-λy-h(x+λ)-k(y-λ)=2λ^{2}-2hλ+2kλ$

$P(2h,2k)$ lies on it:

$2hλ-2kλ-h(2h+λ)-k(2k-λ)=2λ^{2}-2hλ+2kλ$

$\Rightarrow 2λ^{2}-3(h-k)λ+2\left (h^{2}+k^{2}\right )=0$

$P$ is not on $x+y=0$ (its coordinates add to $1$), so each real root gives a genuine chord, and two distinct chords need two distinct real roots:

$9(h-k)^{2}-16\left (h^{2}+k^{2}\right )>0$

Here $h-k=\dfrac{a}{2}$ and $h^{2}+k^{2}=\dfrac{(1+a)^{2}+(1-a)^{2}}{16}=\dfrac{1+a^{2}}{8}$, so

$\dfrac{9a^{2}}{4}-2\left (1+a^{2}\right )>0\Rightarrow a^{2}-8>0\Rightarrow a^{2}\in (8,\infty )$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
Let $\mathrm{A}=[\mathrm{a}_{ij}],\mathrm{a}_{ij}\in \mathrm{ℤ}\cap [0,4],1\leq i,j\leq 2$.

The number of matrices A such that the sum of all entries is a prime number $\mathrm{p}\in (2,13)$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The entries $a_{11},a_{12},a_{21},a_{22}$ are integers from 0 to 4, and their sum must be a prime in $(2,13)$, that is 3, 5, 7 or 11.

For each sum, list the multisets of four entries. A multiset with all entries different gives $4!=24$ matrices, one with exactly one repeated pair gives $\dfrac{4!}{2!}=12$, and one with three equal entries gives $\dfrac{4!}{3!}=4$ (no multiset has two pairs, since each sum is odd).

Sum 3: $\{0,0,0,3\},\{0,0,1,2\},\{0,1,1,1\}$, giving $4+12+4=20$.

Sum 5: $\{0,0,1,4\},\{0,0,2,3\},\{0,1,1,3\},\{0,1,2,2\},\{1,1,1,2\}$, giving $12+12+12+12+4=52$.

Sum 7: $\{0,0,3,4\},\{0,1,2,4\},\{0,1,3,3\},\{0,2,2,3\},\{1,1,1,4\},\{1,1,2,3\},\{1,2,2,2\}$, giving $12+24+12+12+4+12+4=80$.

Sum 11: $\{0,3,4,4\},\{1,2,4,4\},\{1,3,3,4\},\{2,2,3,4\},\{2,3,3,3\}$, giving $12+12+12+12+4=52$ (replacing each entry $a$ by $4-a$ matches these one-to-one with the sum-5 cases).

$\text{Total}=20+52+80+52=204$

Hence, the answer is 204.

text: Let A be the event that the absolute difference between two randomly chosen real numbers in the sample space $[0,60]$ is less than or equal to a . If $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})=\frac{11}{36}$, then $\mathrm{a}$ is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} |\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}|<\mathrm{a}\Rightarrow -\mathrm{a}<\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}<\mathrm{a} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}<\mathrm{a}\text{and}\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}>-\mathrm{a} \end{array}$


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})=\dfrac{\mathrm{ar}(\mathrm{OACDEG})}{(\mathrm{OBDF})} \\  \\ =\dfrac{\mathrm{ar}(\mathrm{OBDF})-\mathrm{ar}(\mathrm{ABC})-\mathrm{ar}(\mathrm{EFG})}{\mathrm{ar}(\mathrm{OBDF})} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{11}{36}=\dfrac{(60)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}(60-\mathrm{a})^{2}-\frac{1}{2}(60-\mathrm{a})^{2}}{3600} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 1100=3600-(60-\mathrm{a})^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow (60-\mathrm{a})^{2}=2500\Rightarrow 60-\mathrm{a}=50 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=10 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
If the constant term in the binomial expansion of $\left (\frac{x^{\dfrac{5}{2}}}{2}-\frac{4}{x^{l}}\right )^{9}$ is $-84$ and the coefficient of $x^{-3l}$ is

$2^{α}β$, where $β<0$ is an odd number, then $|αl-β|$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given binomial expansion of $\left (\frac{x^{\dfrac{5}{2}}}{2}-\frac{4}{x^{l}}\right )^{9}$

$\begin{array}{ll} T_{r+1} & ={}^{9}C_{r}\left (\dfrac{x^{\frac{5}{2}}}{2}\right )^{9-r}\left (\dfrac{-4}{x^{l}}\right )^{r} \\ ={}^{9}C_{r}x^{\frac{45-5r}{2}-lr}\cdot 2^{r-9}\cdot 4^{r}\cdot (-1)^{r} \end{array}$

For constant term, power of x is zero.

So, $\frac{45-5r}{2}=lr\Rightarrow 2lr+5r=45$

Now constant term $=-84$

and ${}^{9}C_{r}\cdot 2^{3r-9}(-1)^{r}=-84$

So, $r=3$ and $l=5$ 

Now for $x^{-15},\frac{45-5r}{2}-5r=-15$

$\Rightarrow$ $45-15r=-30$

$\Rightarrow$ $r=5$

$\therefore$ Coefficient $=-{}^{9}C_{5}2^{6}=-63.2^{7}$

$\therefore α=7,β=-63$

and $|αl-β|=|7\times 5+63|=98$
